developments.title: US tariff of up to 20% on Singapore

for_malaysia: Trade channel: if a key ASEAN hub with a free-trade pact gets up to 20%, Malaysia's target of 19% or less looks like the regional norm rather than a bad deal. Singapore's response also shows the playbook is negotiation, not retaliation.

headline: Singapore said it was 'very disappointed' at a proposed US tariff of up to 20%; the desk could not confirm the STI's close.
numbers_note: No Singapore market numbers could be confirmed from an allowed source this run.

points.text: The US proposed Section 301 tariffs of up to 20% on Singapore. Trade minister Gan Kim Yong said Singapore was 'very disappointed' and disputed the US findings of overcapacity.
For a trade hub with a US trade deficit, this is a political signal more than a direct earnings hit; the rate is still a proposal and open to negotiation.
